pairs.difference: A: the cap sits centred with its board tilted, and it spans most of the width. Its box height of 0.506 is below the real range, but only because a mortarboard is a wide, flat object. B: the boot is whole, tilted slightly toe-down and centred, with all fields in range. Both have clear space on all sides and read instantly at thumbnail size, with nothing competing. The framing gives no reason to choose.

A: the rope coil sits lower left and its loop rises on a diagonal to the upper right, leaving the upper-left corner open. B: the neckerchief is frontal, symmetric and centred, with the round badge as a clear focal point at mid-card. Both fields are in range, both sit floating on a patterned backdrop, and both read at thumbnail size.

A: the jacket and sash fill the card on a diagonal, with balanced height and width and in-range numbers. B: the hat is a low horizontal band with its brim almost reaching both sides. Box height of 0.481 is below the real range and box width of 0.898 is just above it, with empty sunburst above and below. This is only a weak lean, since a hat is naturally wide and it still reads instantly.
pairs.fix: Tilt the hat toward the viewer so the crown looks taller and the brim shows more of its top, filling more of the card's height with less empty background above and below.

pairs.difference: A: the anchor is tilted and centred, a whole object with even clearance. B: the caravan sits in the lower two thirds on grass in three-quarter view, with its right side and hitch closer to the edge and the top third left to the backdrop. Both match real framing types, the floating tilted prop and the grounded object in a set, and both read instantly.

A: the mug sits low in a nearly frontal view, with box height of 0.494 below the real range. The red dot in the middle of the bare silver body pulls the eye at thumbnail size and outranks the mug's own shape, and the bright stripes and table band take up the rest of the card. B: the rose arch is whole and symmetric, and although its box width of 0.90 is slightly over the range, its shape is one clear silhouette with no rival focus.
pairs.fix: Show the cup larger and from a three-quarter view above the table so it fills more of the card height, and remove the single red dot from the middle of the cup.

pairs.difference: A: this is the same computer card shown as REAL in the lessons, so it can be ruled out. B: the saddle is well placed and in range, but the fence rails run across the full card and its post runs up the left edge. They have about the same warm orange-brown value as the saddle, so the fence competes as a second large shape and weakens separation at thumbnail size. The lean comes mostly from A being known real.
pairs.fix: Make the saddle larger and bring it forward, and push the fence back with a paler, softer colour so that only one thin rail shows behind the saddle.

pairs.difference: A: the saloon doors are dead frontal and symmetric, like a flat diagram, and margin of 0.13 is above the real range, leaving a band of empty pink above. The two posts add nothing to the silhouette, so at thumbnail size they read as a square block, not instantly as doors. B: the shoes are a low group with box height of 0.487 below the range, but the angled view reads instantly and matches the low flower-bed card among the real ones. Both have an outlying number, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Turn the doors to a three-quarter view with one door pushed slightly open, make them larger so they fill the card, and leave less empty background above.

pairs.difference: A: the popcorn cart is large and in three-quarter view, with its awning reaching near the top and sides. Box height of 0.869 is slightly over the range, but it has weight and depth. B: the cactus stands dead-centre, frontal and symmetric, a narrow upright with box width of 0.595 below the real range, subject area low at 0.247, and small pebbles arranged around its foot. This is the same centred, whole, upright, base-with-props staging as the generated lighthouse cards.
pairs.fix: Draw the cactus bigger and slightly turned, with its arms of different heights and spread wider, cropped close at the base by the bottom of the card, and remove the small stones.

pairs.difference: A: the barrel is centred, nearly frontal and static, with margin of 0.14 above the real range and width near the bottom of it, so it looks small in its card. The repeated anchor wallpaper adds busy marks all around it at thumbnail size. B: the chest is large at 0.471 area, in three-quarter view with the lid open toward the upper right. Bubbles and coins scatter around it, but the mass of gold stays the clear first read, and all fields are in range.
pairs.fix: Draw the barrel much larger and turned at an angle, seen slightly from above so it fills the card, and replace the anchor wallpaper with a plain soft gradient.

pairs.difference: A: the wagon is whole and fully contained in a tidy three-quarter view. Subject area of 0.50 is above the real range, and it sits packed into the frame with no crop. B: the boat lies on a strong diagonal with the dock cropped by the top and left edges, which is the way real cards let a set run off the card, though the dock and lily pads add secondary shapes and box height of 0.927 is over the range. Both have over-range numbers, so the lean rests on whole versus cropped staging.
pairs.fix: Move in closer so the back wheel and the rear of the canvas run off the card edge, and make the front wheel and canvas opening the main shapes.

pairs.difference: A: the locomotive is whole, neatly fitted inside the card with even clearance, and rests on a horizontal track. This is the fully contained staging seen in generated lessons. B: the coaster is cropped by the left, right and bottom edges, with the track arcing through the frame and the car on a diagonal. It matches the real ferris wheel card's crop. Its box width of 1.0 is over the range only because of that crop.
pairs.fix: Move in closer and tilt the view so the front of the locomotive comes toward the viewer and the cab and rear run off the card edge.

pairs.difference: A: the gloves form a wide low mass spread nearly edge to edge, with box width of 0.951 above the real range, box height of 0.517 below it, and margin of 0.021 just below it. They crowd both sides and leave a dead wall band above. B: the snorkel and mask sit on a strong diagonal with even clearance and all fields in range, and the deck and water are cropped by the corners as a quiet backing. It reads instantly.
pairs.fix: Stack the gloves so one sits upright and overlaps the other, which makes the pair taller and narrower, and centre them with clear space on both sides and above.

pattern: On composition, generated cards are given away mostly by safe staging. The hero is whole and fully contained, parked centrally in a frontal or symmetric view, and often sits on a tidy base with small props around it. Real cards more often let the object or set run off an edge, use a stronger diagonal or three-quarter view, and fill the height of the card. Generated cards also tend to produce box proportions outside the real range: either wide, low bands or narrow uprights with extra margin. Simple bare surfaces can also leave one incidental detail or wallpaper pattern competing for the eye. This signal is weak: several pairs give no composition reason to choose, and the real cards also include centred, whole heroes.
